steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: GCSE Latin verse set texts are prescribed by each exam board and change every two years. Check which texts are current for your exam year.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Common verse authors include Virgil (Aeneid), Ovid (Metamorphoses), Catullus (poems), and Horace (Odes and Satires).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Virgil's Aeneid is the national epic of Rome, telling how Aeneas fled Troy and founded the Roman race in Italy. Key themes: pietas, fate, the cost of empire.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ovid's Metamorphoses tells myths of transformation, often with wit, irony, and playful subversion of epic conventions.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the Aeneid about and who wrote it? | Q: What are the Metamorphoses and what is distinctive about Ovid's approach? | Q: Who was Catullus and what is his poetry about?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: An epic poem by Virgil (29-19 BC) telling how the Trojan hero Aeneas fled Troy, wandered the Mediterranean, and reached Italy to found the Roman race. It explores themes of pietas, fate, and the cost  | Ovid's long narrative poem (AD 8) collecting myths of transformation. Ovid is distinctive for his wit, irony, playful subversion of epic conventions, and sympathetic portrayal of the victims of power. | Catullus (c.84-54 BC) was a Roman lyric poet whose work covers passionate love (poems to Lesbia), friendship, political invective, and social commentary.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always confirm which verse texts are prescribed for YOUR exam year and board. Learn the background of each author: their life, historical period, and reasons for writing. For the Aeneid, know the overall plot even though you only study prescribed passages. Prepare detailed notes on each passage: translation, stylistic features, key themes, and links to the wider work.
